events.summary: The failure MECHANISM is established beyond reasonable doubt and is entirely consumer-side: consumption collapsed at ~07:42Z (61.6→0.4 req/s in the 07:40Z bucket, F7/F14) exactly as lag began climbing monotonically (F8), the first and repeating error is a verbatim deserialization failure on a single offset (orders-3@8841207, 'missing required field qty; schema v1 expected, header says v2', F9), the same offset is then hot-looped with attempt counters ~92k and an explicit 'partition blocked' (F10/F28), CPU pins at 60-71% consistent with busy retry rather than an idle/dead process (F11), and four complete untruncated keyword searches positively remove rebalance/revocation/assignment/session churn (F24-F29, F45). Broker/producer ingress (~2.5k msg/s, F12/F13) and the downstream DB path (pool ~6, p99 ~237ms, ledger-db cpu ~30%, slow_queries ~1/min, F15/F16) are demonstrably undistressed, which independently contradicts and kills H3 and H4, and the metric side shows no second failure mode and no config-related interaction (F42-F47). What is NOT established is the ORIGIN. H1's load-bearing hop — that order-service dep-6010 authored the orders-3 record settlement-service consumes — was put to the specialist as a definitive query in the final round (T7) and returned a definitive negative: no artifact in any available tooling literally binds order-service (or any service) to the 'orders-3' topic or the OrderExecuted stream; payment-service is a documented kafka producer with no topic attribution (F35/F39); the graph edges carry no topic names (F30/F36-F38); dep-6010 names the event but no topic (F40); and no config binds producer to topic (F41). The binding rests on strong field/header naming correlation (qty→quantity, 'venue', header v2 in dep-6010 vs. the consumer error) and the absence of any other producer schema change in the window — not on a declared binding. The data source that would settle it (topic manifest / schema-registry subject→topic mapping / producer deployment descriptor) does not exist in the toolset, so no further query would resolve the origin, and tool budget is exhausted. Two distinct origin questions remain open and would imply different fixes: (a) order-service vs. payment-service as the publisher of orders-3, and (b) whether the offending body is a genuine v2 body (consumer-side deserializer upgrade) or a v1-shaped body mislabeled v2 (producer serialization fix). H1 is still clearly the best-supported origin and its named fix owner (the v2 schema/header transition) is the same either way, but the ranking cannot be defended at the confidence it claims because its decisive hop is unproven by any declaration and unprovable with available data. H2 remains out-competed but not strictly falsified (its two mechanism hops carry no evidence at all), and F19/F23 (error unique to settlement-service) is genuinely ambiguous between 'only settlement-service still asserts schema v1' and 'settlement-service alone misbehaves.'

critiques.summary: H1 remains the only hypothesis whose causal chain is grounded end-to-end on VERIFIED findings: consumer-side stall at onset (61.6→0.4 req/s in the 07:40Z bucket, F7/F14), lag climbing monotonically from ~48 to ~61.6k (F8), verbatim deserialization failure naming a v1/v2 schema mismatch on a single offset (F9), the same offset subsequently hot-looped with attempt counters ~92k and an explicit 'partition blocked' (F10/F28), CPU pinned ~60-71% consistent with busy retry rather than idle/dead (F11), and broker/producer ingress (~2.5k msg/s) plus the downstream DB path (pool ~6, p99 ~237ms, ledger-db cpu ~30%, slow_queries ~1/min) demonstrably undistressed — which independently kills H3 and H4. Round 2 also positively removes H4: four complete, untruncated keyword searches ('rebalanc','revok','assign','session','group') return zero, so round 1's truncation caveat no longer applies (F24-F29, T6). The remaining blocking gap is unchanged: the single load-bearing hop — that order-service dep-6010 authored the orders-3 record — is still an assumption. F31/F30 show order-service holds a queue-produce edge into the shared kafka broker and payment-service is an equally-plausible unexamined publisher of the same stream (F35), and no declared topic binding for orders-3 exists. The confidence the evidence supports rests on strong naming/field correlation (qty→quantity, 'venue', header v2 in dep-6010 vs. the consumer error), not on a producer→orders-3 link. H2 is out-competed but not strictly falsified: two of its hops carry no evidence at all, and T5's finding that the deserialization error is unique to settlement-service (F19/F23) is ambiguous — it is equally consistent with 'only settlement-service still asserts schema v1' (H1) and 'settlement-service alone is misbehaving' (H2). Two cheap, decisive queries remain: pin the producer→orders-3 binding, and get settlement-service error_rate/restarts, which was explicitly asked and never answered.

F6 shows the graph exposes no upstream producer edge for settlement-service; F30/F31 give order-service a generic kafka queue-produce edge with no topic attribute; F35 leaves payment-service as an unexamined alternative publisher of the same stream. The link rests entirely on naming correlation (qty→quantity, 'venue', header v2) with no declared orders-3 binding. This is the hop that determines whether the fix owner is order-service.

A revert/falsification test on cfg-3004, or a per-producer counter, would settle it.

No measurement contradicts a poll-batch change slowing throughput to ~0; the only counter-evidence is that the observed mechanism is a single-offset poison loop. Weak but not eliminated by observation alone.

The 'healthy' verdicts for the downstream DB path (F15/F16) and broker (F12/F13) sometimes rest on one to two series each (pool+latency; one ingress metric). They are consistent across independent series but not exhaustive — e.g. no direct lock/wait metric exists for ledger-db. This is acceptable for ruling out H3/H4 but should not be over-stated.

critiques.summary: The failure MECHANISM is established beyond reasonable doubt and is entirely consumer-side: consumption collapsed at ~07:42Z (61.6→0.4 req/s in the 07:40Z bucket, F7/F14) exactly as lag began climbing monotonically (F8), the first and repeating error is a verbatim deserialization failure on a single offset (orders-3@8841207, 'missing required field qty; schema v1 expected, header says v2', F9), the same offset is then hot-looped with attempt counters ~92k and an explicit 'partition blocked' (F10/F28), CPU pins at 60-71% consistent with busy retry rather than an idle/dead process (F11), and four complete untruncated keyword searches positively remove rebalance/revocation/assignment/session churn (F24-F29, F45). Broker/producer ingress (~2.5k msg/s, F12/F13) and the downstream DB path (pool ~6, p99 ~237ms, ledger-db cpu ~30%, slow_queries ~1/min, F15/F16) are demonstrably undistressed, which independently contradicts and kills H3 and H4, and the metric side shows no second failure mode and no config-related interaction (F42-F47). What is NOT established is the ORIGIN. H1's load-bearing hop — that order-service dep-6010 authored the orders-3 record settlement-service consumes — was put to the specialist as a definitive query in the final round (T7) and returned a definitive negative: no artifact in any available tooling literally binds order-service (or any service) to the 'orders-3' topic or the OrderExecuted stream; payment-service is a documented kafka producer with no topic attribution (F35/F39); the graph edges carry no topic names (F30/F36-F38); dep-6010 names the event but no topic (F40); and no config binds producer to topic (F41). The binding rests on strong field/header naming correlation (qty→quantity, 'venue', header v2 in dep-6010 vs. the consumer error) and the absence of any other producer schema change in the window — not on a declared binding. The data source that would settle it (topic manifest / schema-registry subject→topic mapping / producer deployment descriptor) does not exist in the toolset, so no further query would resolve the origin, and tool budget is exhausted. Two distinct origin questions remain open and would imply different fixes: (a) order-service vs. payment-service as the publisher of orders-3, and (b) whether the offending body is a genuine v2 body (consumer-side deserializer upgrade) or a v1-shaped body mislabeled v2 (producer serialization fix). H1 is still clearly the best-supported origin and its named fix owner (the v2 schema/header transition) is the same either way, but the ranking cannot be defended at the confidence it claims because its decisive hop is unproven by any declaration and unprovable with available data. H2 remains out-competed but not strictly falsified (its two mechanism hops carry no evidence at all), and F19/F23 (error unique to settlement-service) is genuinely ambiguous between 'only settlement-service still asserts schema v1' and 'settlement-service alone misbehaves.'

challenges.issue: The load-bearing producer→topic hop (order-service authored the orders-3/OrderExecuted record settlement-service consumes) is not verified by any declaration. The final definitive query (T7) returned an explicit negative: no manifest, schema-registry mapping, graph topic attribute, deploy record, config, or historical artifact binds any producer to orders-3; the link rests only on field/header naming correlation and the absence of another producer schema change. With the decisive data source absent from the toolset and budget exhausted, this hop cannot be closed.

payment-service is an equally documented kafka producer (F30/F35/F39) with no topic attribution, so it cannot be excluded as the publisher of the orders-3 stream; the separation would require a per-producer/per-topic counter or a payment-service schema check, neither of which was obtainable.

The open detail (genuine v2 body vs. v1-shaped body mislabeled v2) determines whether the fix is a consumer deserializer upgrade or a producer serialization fix. It is treated as fix-neutral because the owner is the same, but it is a distinguishable origin statement with different corrective actions and is unresolved.

Not strictly falsified: both mechanism hops (smaller poll batches driving throughput to ~0; the config altering retry timing without a group signature) carry zero evidence, and F19/F23's uniqueness of the deserialization error to settlement-service is genuinely readable both ways. H2 is out-competed rather than contradicted.

Rejection is indirect — no lock/wait or connection-saturation metric exists for ledger-db; ruled out only via flat CPU/slow_queries and flat consumer pool/latency rather than a direct lock metric. Consistent across four series, so the rejection stands, but it is inferential.

Calibration: the stated 0.66 confidence is defensible for the mechanism but over-weighted for the origin, given that the single decisive hop was affirmatively found to be undocumented and unavailable. Cap set at 0.72 to reflect 'best origin, unproven binding.'
